objective:
In a fresh worktree /Users/FradSer/Developer/FradSer/git-agent/git-agent-intent on a new branch feat/staged-boundaries cut from develop, git-agent acts only on the split boundary the user has already expressed in the index, and reports when a file could be split, instead of inferring regions.

What must be true when this is met:

1. A run whose index already holds changes commits exactly the index content as its first commit, from the diff the index holds, without unstaging or re-staging anything. The defect reproduced on develop — a hand-staged region followed by `git commit --no-stage` puts unstaged work into the commit — does not happen. The unstaged remainder of the same file stays out of that commit.
2. `--no-stage` commits exactly what the index holds and nothing else, which is what its own help text already claims.
3. After that first commit, the remaining changes follow the existing file-level flow unchanged, so a run with an empty index behaves exactly as develop does.
4. When a changed file's own diff covers two or more git-anchored regions, the run reports that fact and names the regions and the command that splits them (`git add -p`), on the warning stream a scripted run also receives. No region is inferred, no content is rebuilt, and no index entry is written by git-agent itself.
5. No region policy remains: there is no gap, no size floor, no hunk inventory, no applier, no ledger, and nothing left to tune or measure. The production code this feature adds is a few hundred lines at most, and the model-free split measurement harness is not needed by it.
6. The working tree is never written to, and a preview (`--dry-run`) shows the same commits without committing.
7. Whole-file behavior for a run whose index is empty is byte-identical to develop: same prompts, same exit codes, same JSON fields, same commit content.

The branch carries a written comparison against feat/hunk-staging: production lines added, the behavior difference on the reproduced case, the risk each approach carries, and what the earlier measurement says about each.

summary:
The alternative approach is implemented, verified and committed on a fresh worktree: /Users/FradSer/Developer/FradSer/git-agent/git-agent-intent, branch feat/staged-boundaries cut from develop (6c58d09), commit 527af48 "feat(app): commit the index as staged". 18 packages ok, 0 FAIL. develop and the hunk worktree are untouched.

WHAT IT DOES
The index is the only split the run acts on. A run whose index holds changes commits exactly that content, first, from the diff the index holds: `git commit` on the index, no unstage, no restage, no content rebuilt, no index entry written by git-agent. The remainder (the working tree against the index, plus untracked files) then goes through the existing file-level flow unchanged. When a file the run is about to commit whole holds two or more git-anchored regions, the run reports that on the warning stream, names the regions and points at `git add -p <file>`; it never splits on its own.

EVIDENCE BY CONTRACT ITEM

1. gofmt / build / suite: `gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `make build` succeeds; `make test` reports 18 packages ok and 0 FAIL lines.

2. The develop defect and its fix, both recorded this session with the same fixture (only the func Beta region staged by hand, the func Epsilon change loose):
   - develop binary, `--no-stage`: HEAD carried `-return "beta"`/`+return "BETA"` AND `-return "epsilon"`/`+return "EPSILON"`, and no unstaged file was left — the defect, reproduced.
   - intent binary, same input: HEAD carried only the beta change, and `git diff --name-only` still listed app.go — the unstaged remainder stayed out.
   - On the branch, TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_KeepsTheStagedRegionApart PASS (4.94s) asserts the first commit holds the staged region and not the working tree change, that the second commit holds the remainder alone, and that the tree ends clean.

3. `--no-stage` commits the index and nothing else: TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_NoStageCommitsTheIndexOnly PASS (1.99s) asserts one new commit, the index empty afterwards, and `git diff` still holding the unstaged region.

4. Empty-index parity: the two-binary differential on the same fixture with an empty index prints "(identical commit subjects)" and "JSON ENVELOPE: IDENTICAL" after blanking SHAs. On the branch, a run whose index is empty takes exactly develop's path: the same plan inputs (`staged` empty, `unstaged` = the changed files), the same prompts, the same JSON fields.

5. The report: TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_ReportsAMultiRegionFile PASS (3.27s) asserts stderr carries "holds 2 separate regions" and "git add -p app.go", and that the run still commits one commit rather than splitting on its own; TestCommitCmd_StagedBoundary_SingleRegionIsNotReported PASS (4.09s) asserts a single-region change produces no such line. The stream is `WarnWriter`, which cmd wires to `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` unconditionally, so a scripted run reads it.

6. No region policy remains: no gap, no size floor, no hunk inventory, no applier, no ledger, no content hash writer. Production lines added, measured against develop: application/commit_service.go 100, application/staged_boundary.go 219, cmd/commit.go 3, infrastructure/git/client.go 26 — 348 in total, against 1447 on feat/hunk-staging. There is nothing to tune, so the model-free split measurement harness is not needed by it.

7. The written comparison is in the branch at .memory/staged-boundaries-instead-of-inferred-regions.md: production and test lines for both approaches, what each acts on, what each needs, the settings each has, the defect each fixes, the defect each can create, and what the earlier measurement says about each. README and CHANGELOG state the behaviour.

FOUND WHILE DOING IT
The staged-content path initially sent the staged diff to the model without the content filter or the byte cap. The full suite caught it (`TestCommitService_ByteCapAppliedBeforeGenerate`: "diff sent to LLM is 786432 bytes, exceeds cap 393216"). The filter-and-cap tail of `prepareGroup` is now `preparedForModel`, shared by both paths, and both cap warnings go to the warning stream. Two more fixture-level consequences of the deliberate change were fixed honestly rather than by loosening an assertion: the judgment fixtures now start from an empty index (the situation those seams run in), and the two autonomous-root stubs build their plan from the files the prompt listed instead of a hardcoded path.

LIMITS
The behaviour change reaches every run whose index holds changes, not only `--no-stage`: such a run now makes one more commit than before, because the staged content is its own commit rather than being merged into the first group. That is the point of the approach (the staged boundary is committed exactly), it is stated in the README and the CHANGELOG, and it is why six existing fixtures changed. Nothing in the approach checks that the resulting commits build, which is the same boundary the other approach also kept, and here it is weaker in scope: the run only ever commits content the user staged plus whole files the file-level flow already committed.
